narration._comment: Authored whole per locale. Arabic number-noun agreement is irregular (dual for 2, a broken plural for 3-10, a singular accusative for 11+), so a sentence built by substituting a count into a template produces wrong Arabic. The validator rejects a {count} placeholder in an ar string for exactly this reason - which is also why every round below carries its OWN authored prompt and reveal rather than one template reused three times.

hint1.en: Touch each one as you count it.

hint2.en: Let's count together, one at a time.

model.en: Watch me count them, then you try.

success.en: Nine watchers in all. That is nine clues!
success.ar: تِسْعَةُ مُرَاقِبِينَ فِي المَجْمُوع. تِسْعَةُ أَدِلَّة!

payload._comment: tenFrame sits second on the arrangement ladder (dice, tenFrame, linear, scatter, random). It is the right place to start a first Adventure: structured enough to support the one-to-one sweep, not so structured that it gives the answer away.
payload._roundsComment: Authored rounds, not a random count in a range. Three reasons, all of them story reasons: the counts are FIXED so the next beat can truthfully say 'nine watchers'; each round names its own animal so no two rounds of the same activity ask the same question; and the totals differ (3, 4, 2) so a child cannot answer the second round from the first. A randomised countRange gave none of that and could repeat the same number three times in a row.

prompt.en: How many monkeys are up in the branches?

revealLine.en: Three monkeys saw it go by.

prompt.en: How many birds are watching from the sky?

revealLine.en: Four birds saw it go by.

prompt.en: How many rabbits are hiding in the grass?

revealLine.en: Two rabbits saw it go by.
